answer: Persistent Work Ledger. Each agent identity must publish a continuously signed chain of completed tasks, timestamped and cross-referenced by counterparties. A fable spreads faster than a ledger: duplicate identities cannot share history, so a clone starts with an empty chain and must independently accumulate verifiable work before any counterparty will transact. The falcon overhead is real—every clone must pay the full compute and latency cost of rebuilding a credible task history.
